item.title: Taxis face checks in county-wide police operation
item.description: Norfolk Police have confirmed that taxis and private hire vehicles will be part of a nationwide commercial vehicle enforcement campaign running from 26 January to 8 February. The operation, led by the National Police Chiefs’ Council, is aimed at vehicles used for business and trade and will see police forces across the country intensify checks on a wide range of commercial drivers. item.title: DRIVING UP COSTS: Taxi fleets report surge in airport drop-off debt recovery demands without prior notices
item.description: London taxi rental firms are reporting a growing volume of debt recovery demands linked to airport enforcement notices they say were never previously issued, raising concerns about process failures affecting both fleets and owner drivers. One large black cab rental operator told TaxiPoint it is now receiving an average of 10 to 15 debt recovery letters each week relating to alleged parking or traffic contraventions at Heathrow, Luton and Stansted airports. item.title: From 6am rides to 4am takeaways, Uber maps how Britain really moves
item.description: New data released by Uber, based on millions of trips and deliveries across the UK, shows clear regional contrasts in how people travel, eat and socialise, with major implications for mobility providers, local authorities and the night-time economy. Edinburgh recorded the highest proportion of late-night trips in 2025, with journeys between 10pm and 4am accounting for a larger share of rides than in any other UK city. item.title: Crawley Council FREEZES taxi licensing fees despite inflation pressures
item.description: Crawley Borough Council has confirmed it will not increase Hackney Carriage and Private Hire licensing fees and charges for the coming year, holding costs steady for the local taxi trade. The decision comes at a time when inflation remains above zero, meaning the fee freeze represents an effective real terms reduction for licensed drivers and operators, easing some of the financial pressure facing the sector. The council said the move follows a full review of its taxi and private hire...

item.title: Taxi drivers among five charged in NCA probe into migrant smuggling network
item.description: Image credit: NCA Five people, including three licensed taxi drivers, have been charged following a National Crime Agency investigation into a suspected organised crime group accused of smuggling migrants out of the UK in lorries. The operation followed two days of surveillance on Monday 26 and Tuesday 27 January, during which investigators observed a number of taxis travelling from London to a location near Whitstable in Kent. item.title: Elderly taxi passenger seriously injured in West Moors collision
item.description: Dorset Police are appealing for witnesses after a serious injury collision involving a taxi in West Moors that left an elderly passenger hospitalised. Officers were called at 1.37pm on Friday 23 January 2026 to a collision between a blue Volkswagen Caddy taxi and a silver Ford B-Max at the junction of Station Road and Denewood Road. item.description: Image credit: WV Public Protection Taxi licensing officers from City of Wolverhampton Council carried out enforcement checks in Dudley on Tuesday as part of a joint operation with West Midlands Police and Dudley Metropolitan Borough Council. The operation involved roadside vehicle inspections, with licensed taxis stopped and checked for compliance with licensing and road safety requirements. item.title: Cabbidder appoints James Sorolla as CTO to speed dispatch integrations across UK taxi sector
item.description: Cabbidder has appointed James Sorolla as Chief Technology Officer and a board member, tasking him with accelerating platform development and integrations with dispatch systems across the UK taxi and private hire sector. Sorolla will oversee enhancements to the existing Cabbidder platform and the delivery of a new Cabbidder sharing hub. item.title: TOP TAXI: Freenow opens search for London’s top black cab drivers
item.description: Image credit: Freenow by Lyft Freenow by Lyft has opened nominations for a London-focused driver recognition event aimed at celebrating black cab drivers who delivered outstanding service to passengers and communities during 2025.
